items.passage: During the renovation, the archive remained open to researchers. However, one quiet corner was reserved for technicians who were cleaning fragile maps, so visitors were asked to work elsewhere.
choices: set aside for a particular use

items.passage: Engineers tested an older protective coating by pressing it with a rounded tool. Under gentle pressure, the coating yielded, revealing that it had become softer over time.

Committee members initially praised the architect’s proposal, and some urged construction of the entire complex at once. After cost estimates arrived, the members tempered their support: they endorsed the central hall but asked to defer two wings.

The curator’s attribution had rested mainly on a stylistic resemblance and was therefore disputed. Newly cataloged shipping records showed repeated deliveries from the artist’s usual supplier to the workshop, evidence that sustained the attribution.

The critic began by calling the exhibition inventive. She then noted that several interactive displays lacked clear instructions and concluded that only the installations with guides fully succeeded. Those reservations qualified her praise.

Young ravens initially repeated one familiar route to a food container. When researchers blocked that route, however, the birds tried alternatives, and after the barrier was removed, some selected whichever route was shorter. The researchers described this behavior as plastic.
The researchers found promising traces of pollen in the soil, but they reserved judgment about the site’s former vegetation until a second laboratory could analyze the samples.
choices: held back until more information was available

items.passage: After the small publisher received advance orders from several bookstores, its prospects for covering the printing costs looked bright.
A search of the town archive yielded two letters describing the original clock tower. Until then, historians had only a sketch of the structure.
The pond’s water level remained stable through the dry week. Daily measurements varied by less than one centimeter.
choices: kept in a building for horses

items.passage: Rather than relying on annual averages, the ecologist used fine-grained measurements taken every fifteen minutes. This detailed record revealed brief temperature spikes that the averages had hidden.
Managers hoped the new drainage channel would check the spread of standing water across the field. After the first storm, flooding stopped at the channel’s edge.
The review panel agreed that the field survey was carefully conducted, but it asked the authors to temper their confident conclusion because observations covered only one migration season.
The proposal that the marks were a counting system initially drew little attention. It gained currency only after similar marks were documented at three neighboring sites.
choices: rapid movement from place to place

items.passage: The committee’s endorsement of the riverfront plan was qualified: members supported restoring the wetland but withheld approval of the proposed footbridge until engineers assessed its effect on floodwater.
choices: limited by a condition or reservation

items.passage: Although earlier petitions had been denied, the council voted to sanction the excavation after researchers agreed to cap exposed walls each evening and publish monthly condition reports.
A brief comic anecdote gives the otherwise solemn essay an ironic inflection: the author’s conclusion remains serious, but it now sounds less severe and more self-aware.
choices: grammatical ending added to a word
change in vocal pitch during speech
subtle modification in tone or meaning
bias that makes an account unreliable

items.passage: One ambiguous inscription cannot sustain the claim that the settlement had its own mint, but the inscription combined with metal molds and unfinished coins may support a narrower version of that argument.
choices: keep at a fixed physical height

items.passage: Repeated winter floods had carried soil away from the garden beds. After volunteers planted dense rows of native grass along the slope, the roots arrested much of the erosion, and far less soil reached the path below.
At first, the mineral streaks on the cave wall looked faint. Under angled light, however, their branching pattern became pronounced enough for the survey team to trace each line in a photograph.

The archive once treated the architect’s sketches as a single continuous series. New analysis shows that the pages belong to three discrete groups: early pencil studies, later ink revisions, and presentation drawings produced after construction began.

Instead of releasing rainwater directly onto the plaza, the roof’s shallow grooves channeled it toward planted basins. Sensors showed that most runoff reached the basins before entering the storm drain.

A layer of airborne ash initially blocked much of the sensor’s radio signal. After rain removed particles from the air, the interference was attenuated, allowing the receiver to detect weaker transmissions.
The marsh’s dense reeds conferred an advantage on young herons: hidden among the stalks, the birds could approach small fish without being seen. Herons hunting along bare banks caught fewer fish.
Before the storm, workers fixed each solar panel to the frame with two additional clamps so that high winds could not lift it.
As the warm air rose through the tower, cooler air was drawn through vents near the floor, keeping the room comfortable without a fan.
The difference between the two coatings was marked: one remained clear after a month outdoors, whereas the other became cloudy within a week.
The research team conducted three trials at each temperature, recording the time required for the material to harden.
A thin mineral coating rendered the clay vessel nearly waterproof, allowing it to hold oil without leaking.
Owls can locate faint rustling beneath leaves because their acute hearing detects small differences in when sound reaches each ear.
A dense clay layer mediated the exchange of water between the wetland and the aquifer, slowing infiltration after storms and limiting upward seepage during dry periods.
The architect chose a spare interior: bare plaster walls, simple wooden benches, and almost no decorative trim.
The newly discovered ledger has direct bearing on the dispute because its dated entries show who controlled the warehouse during the contested year.
The repair crew worked with dispatch, replacing the damaged hinge and reopening the gate before the morning deliveries arrived.
Producing the instrument’s thin ceramic reeds was exacting work: a difference of less than a millimeter could alter the pitch enough to spoil the entire set.
The committee considered the estimate sound because it drew on three independent surveys and produced similar results under different assumptions.

The committee never formally voted to prioritize the roof repair. Nevertheless, every proposed budget placed that repair first, and no member objected. The repeated choices revealed a tacit agreement about which work was most urgent.
choices: lasting for only a short time

items.passage: The reviewer's brief comments identified two hidden assumptions that had distorted the cost estimate and proposed a test that would separate their effects. Her colleagues valued the analysis because it was incisive.

A survey of three sheltered coves initially led researchers to claim that juvenile fish avoid all exposed shorelines. After a wider survey found abundant juveniles beside several wave-battered reefs, the team circumscribed its claim: avoidance was evident only where exposed shores also lacked rock crevices.

One shipyard ledger dated a launch to April, while a harbor log appeared to place the same event in May. An archivist discovered that the harbor clerk recorded dates only when vessels cleared inspection. By distinguishing launch from clearance, she reconciled the two records within a single timeline.

The fossil's tooth pattern resembled that of a known river-dwelling reptile, but the surrounding rock had been transported from another site. The museum therefore used a provisional species label until chemical tests could establish where the fossil was originally buried.

Two mountain footpaths share the same stone paving and grade, so those features cannot identify which route appears in an undated photograph. A drainage lip visible along only the eastern path is therefore the most salient detail for assigning the image to a route.
During the public meeting, engineer Laila Chen fielded questions about the bridge design and explained how the new supports would be inspected.
When several cracks appeared in the footbridge deck, the sudden damage prompted engineers to close the bridge for inspection.
Finding the same mineral signature in samples from three valleys provided substantial evidence that ash from one eruption reached the entire region.
For the restoration team, the critical feature of the old gate was its hinge spacing; a replacement with different spacing would not fit the original posts.

Asked whether a newly found pigment proved that two workshops exchanged materials, chemist Elena Rivera gave a circumspect answer. The chemical match was suggestive, she said, but the samples were too few to establish regular exchange.
Tree-ring dates placed the cabin's construction around 1760. A tax ledger from 1761 named the same owner and described a cabin on that parcel, so the ledger corroborated the physical evidence.
News of the signal excited the observatory, yet its director gave a measured response. She emphasized that equipment noise had not been fully excluded and requested another month of data.
Although the report contained extensive measurements, its explanation of how the variables interacted remained opaque to readers outside the specialty.
At room temperature, the dried reed snapped under pressure. After a brief steam treatment, however, it became yielding and could curve around the basket frame.
The first calibration produced a tentative estimate. Engineers would revise the value if the longer test revealed additional sensor drift.
The two recordings sounded identical through laptop speakers, but trained listeners could register a slight difference when using studio headphones.
Solar panels normally powered the remote weather station. During a string of cloudy days, a backup battery could tide the station over, keeping its instruments active until sunlight returned.
choices: support it through a temporary period
